newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China to send more PLA troops to Hong Kong Friday.
newsitem.headline: China to send more PLA troops to Hong Kong Friday.

text.p: China will send 90 People's Liberation Army soldiers to Hong Kong on Friday to beef up an advance party preparing to take over from withdrawing British troops when the territory changes hands.
The third batch of personnel for Beijing's future garrison will arrive at the Lok Ma Chau land frontier post from China's Shenzhen region, a military spokesman said on Tuesday.
China would then have 206 military personnel in Hong Kong laying the ground for Beijing's takeover at midnight on June 30, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
A first batch of 40 troops, led by Major-General Zhou Borong, arrived on April 21, and 66 came in on May 19.
Under a 1984 Sino-British handover treaty, Hong Kong will become a special region of China free to run all its own affairs except defence and diplomacy.

Britain has been steadily winding down its military presence in Hong Kong. Only 1,000 military and civilian personnel remain in the British garrison, down from 10,000 in its heyday several years ago. The remaining defence forces include 400 soldiers of the Black Watch regiment.
China has promised to send handpicked elite troops whose good behaviour in the territory will be guaranteed.
However, many of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people have stark memories of the PLA's actions in 1989 when tanks rolled into Beijing's Tiananmen Square to crush a student protest movement.
